title: Proper reduced connected subgroups of PGL2 are solvable
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All groups are affine $F$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and all subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Let $I\subsetneq\operatorname{PGL}_{2,F}$ be a proper closed subgroup scheme, where $\operatorname{PGL}_{2,F}$ is the projective matrix group of [lem-sfb-projective-matrix-central-cover]. Assume $I$ is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme] and connected [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Then $I$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and solvable, meaning that successive scheme-theoretic commutator subgroup schemes eventually become trivial. No characteristic restriction is imposed.

source.place: Corollary 17.27, printed p.360, together with the smooth reduction theorem over a perfect field and dimension three of PGL2; used in Theorem 20.16 (c) implies (d), printed p.413.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-locally-algebraic-group-identity-component] to $I$. Since $I$ is connected, its identity component $I^0$, with the open-subscheme structure supplied there, is all of $I$. Since $I$ is reduced, its nilradical is zero, so $(I^0)_{\mathrm{red}}=I$ by [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]. The cited identity-component theorem says that this reduced component is smooth and integral. In particular $I$ is smooth; no characteristic-zero theorem is being used.

source.place: Tag 0B7R, proposition-connected-component; Tags 047R, lemma-reduced-subgroup-scheme-perfect, 047P, lemma-reduced-group-scheme-prefect-field-characteristic-p-smooth, and 047N, lemma-group-scheme-characteristic-zero-smooth; Milne Proposition 1.26, printed p.13.

proof.text: Put $P=\operatorname{PGL}_{2,F}$. By [lem-sfb-projective-matrix-central-cover], $P$ is affine, smooth, connected and of dimension $2^2-1=3$. Applying [lem-sfb-locally-algebraic-group-identity-component] to the connected group $P$ shows that $P=P^0$ is irreducible. Smoothness gives reducedness by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced]. The identity section makes $P$ nonempty, so it is integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. The underlying closed subset $|I|$ is proper in $|P|$: otherwise write the closed immersion into the affine scheme $P=\operatorname{Spec}A$ as $\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$ by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The ring $A$ is a domain by integrality. If $V(J)=\operatorname{Spec}A$, its prime ideal $(0)$ contains $J$, so $J=0$; this would give $I=P$, contrary to the hypothesis. Every chain of irreducible closed subsets of $|I|$ is a chain of closed subsets of $|P|$, and appending the strictly larger irreducible closed subset $|P|$ increases its length by one. Thus the definition of Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] gives $\dim I+1\leq3$, so $\dim I\leq2$.

source.place: Theorem 20.16(c) implies (d), printed p.413, proper-image dimension argument made explicit. Stacks Tag 056T, lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal, for reducedness; Tag 01QO, lemma-closed-immersion, for the quotient-ring description.

proof.text: The group $I$ is affine and of finite type by hypothesis, connected by hypothesis, smooth by step 1, and has dimension at most two by step 2. Apply [lem-sfb-connected-group-dimension-two-solvable] with $k=F$ and $G=I$. Its conclusion is termination of the scheme-theoretic derived series, exactly the solvability required here. Together with step 1 this proves both assertions.
